FIGURE: [description of the image, not printed words] A table titled “TABLE 1.1 Rainfall Intensity Data Recorded over a Period of 29 Years” has three paired columns labelled “Year No.” and “Rainfall Intensity, in.”, listing years 1–29 with numerical values. Beneath it are four centered equations: x̄ = 1/29 (43.30 + ⋯ + 43.11) = 50.70 in.; s²ₓ = 1/29 [(43.30 − 50.70)² + ⋯ + (43.11 − 50.70)²] = 57.34; sₓ = 7.57 in.; and sₓ̄ = 7.57/√29 = 1.41 in.

novice.takeaway: For 29 years of rainfall data, the average is 50.70 inches, the values vary by 7.57 inches, and the sample-average uncertainty is 1.41 inches.
questions: What does epistemic uncertainty mean here?
novice.inferred_claim: The standard error describes uncertainty in the estimated average rainfall.

peer.takeaway: For 29 annual rainfall-intensity observations, the mean is 50.70 in., standard deviation is 7.57 in., and the sample-mean sampling error is 1.41 in.
peer.inferred_claim: Sampling error quantifies epistemic uncertainty in the estimated mean rainfall intensity.

expert.takeaway: For 29 annual rainfall intensities, the mean is 50.70 in., standard deviation 7.57 in., and standard error of the mean 1.41 in., representing epistemic uncertainty in the estimated average.
expert.inferred_claim: The standard error quantifies uncertainty in the estimated mean annual rainfall intensity.
